about: THE CARDS OF THE RHINE AND FRISIA (region rhine_frisia: Dorestad, Traiectum, Witla, Walichrum, Noviomagus, Daventre, Medemelacha, Winaldum, Doccinga, Emuthon). Written 6 Oct 2026 by the region's weaver from the ports' places files (Data/places/<port>.json), the dossiers (Design/content/dossiers) and the spine (Design/content/spine.json). A draft in the game's own files, for the user to overwrite. Each card names its port with port.id in its 'when' and is listed in its site's 'do' in the places file. The words are in Data/writing/rhine_frisia.json under rhine_frisia.<port>.<card>.<slot>; a picture line for each card is there as art.<card id>. The spine's thread flags are set only for the step they name; this file's own flags begin rf_ (two places-file flags are kept as they were: traiectum_chest_aboard, traiectum_chest_saved). Grand rewards are unlock_ flags (Design/content/CHAINS.md). Small lines run through several ports: the bundles (Dorestad, Medemelacha, Emuthon), the bell (Daventre, Traiectum), the cup (Winaldum, Traiectum), the salve (Walichrum, Emuthon), the smith's silver (Daventre, Noviomagus), the book (Dorestad, Traiectum), the priests (Emuthon, Traiectum), the old pennies (Walichrum, Dorestad), the count's word (Walichrum, Noviomagus), the chest (Traiectum, Daventre), the huntsman's word (Noviomagus, Daventre), the false news of Offa (Walichrum, Dorestad). A second batch of 24 cards was added on 7 Oct 2026 (from harbour.gate_bench.traiectum to the end of the file), so that the chief sites of the large ports each have a card of their own and the later years have some: its lines through several ports are the captive (Noviomagus, Daventre, 880-881), the hostages' tally (Daventre, Noviomagus), the news of Rodulf (Doccinga, Daventre, 873), the coffin (after the salve: Walichrum), and the notched stick (Medemelacha, 839 and 842). Every source is in the card's 'note'; (?) marks what was not checked. A third batch was added on the morning of 7 Oct 2026 (from harbour.painted_leaf.dorestad to the end of the file) by the weaver who finished the region: the hooks of the spine that had a story and no card (the psalter leaf, the king's ships of 797, the Saxon who ran, the news of Godfred's death, Catla's purse, the last seasons of Witla, Harald's island, Rorik before King Charles in 870), the sites of the large ports that had no card of their own (the barge bank, the Vecht side, the bishop's mint, Adelbold's cathedral, the ring wall, the earth wall, the weirs, the mints of Daventre, Doccinga and Emuthon), and the later years to 1063. Its lines through several ports are the painted leaf (Dorestad, Traiectum), the count of keels (Witla, Dorestad, 834-836), the saint's tenth (Medemelacha, Traiectum and back) and the cousins' dye (Winaldum, Emuthon). One card is opened only by another (harbour.catlas_bag.dorestad, by the 'then' of harbour.catlas_purse.dorestad). The thread flags it sets for the first time anywhere are hy_ran_grain (Emuthon) and, in this file, lf_trail_north, bk_parchment, df_warned, df_rorik_man and sx_carried_fugitive.

cards.note: Dorestad, the dam heads: Ravn (dorestad.ravn, cast.crew.ravn) sets the first riddle of the old hall contest, r-gest-01 (ale), and gives the stanza of the names of ale (t-alv-34) when it is answered. The spine's thread riddle_road, hook for Dorestad; the story dorestad.first_question, beat 1. Source: riddles_793.json 'start' and r-gest-01 (Heidreks gátur 1); the stanza is Alvíssmál 34 (Bellows 1923), in texts_793.json.

cards.note: Dorestad, Thiadburg's storehouse (dorestad.thiadburg, cast.thiadburg). She tells of the blood owed at York (sets yk_feud_known: thread york_blood, hook for Dorestad; story dorestad.radgers_price beat 1) and will stand surety for a house she trusts (sets db_surety: thread counts_day; story dorestad.michaelmas beat 3). Both are invented on the spine's frame; the real ground is Altfrid, Vita Liudgeri I.11-12 (the Frisian merchant's killing at York and the flight of the Frisians, about 773). Cloth at 42 d the bolt is a friend's price (goods_793.json frisian_cloth 48 d).

cards.note: Dorestad, Thiadbod's dam head (dorestad.thiadbod, cast.thiadbod): he asks you to lie a night at the eel stakes below Medemelacha. First card of three (then harbour.eel_stakes.medemelacha and harbour.night_hull.emuthon): the thread swords_north, hooks for Dorestad, Medemelacha and Emuthon; the story medemelacha.night_boats beat 1. The law behind it: no mail out of the realm (Herstal 779, c. 20), no arms to merchants (803), nothing east but by the border posts (Thionville 805). The people and the cargo are invented.

cards.note: Dorestad, the upper church: the priest (dorestad.priest, Alfward) has the news of Lindisfarne (8 June 793: Anglo-Saxon Chronicle 793; Alcuin's letters) and a book for the bishop at Traiectum. The thread holy_island, hook for Dorestad, and the start of the book road; the story dorestad.letter_from_york beat 1. Delivered by harbour.school_chest.traiectum. cards.note: Dorestad, the hall at De Geer: a lawsuit. A skipper claims damage to his barge and the steward (dorestad.hartwin, cast.hartwin) hears it for the count, who is with the host (thread saxon_end, hook for Dorestad: 'his steward keeps the tally'). Clearing oneself by oath with oath-helpers is the Frisian law's ordinary proof (Lex Frisionum, passim: 'cum sex sacramentalibus iuret' and the like, c. 802 (?)). The case, the sum and the people are invented.

cards.note: Dorestad, Aldswith's house (dorestad.aldswith): where news is heard. A rumour that is TRUE: in the hungry year the terps have no bread and pay for rye in cloth (thread hungry_years, hook for Wijnaldum 'also at Doccinga, Emuthon and Medemelacha'; the famine of 792-793: Annales Mosellani, Laureshamenses). She also puts right the FALSE rumour of harbour.wiltruds_house.walichrum (flag rf_heard_offa_dead: Offa died on 29 July 796, not before). The line about Thiadbod's steersman is the story dorestad.casks_that_ring beat 2. A merchant's son schooled at Utrecht sells the anchor riddle (riddle_symphosius_61_ancora: thread riddle_road, hook for Dorestad; story dorestad.first_question beat 3); his words are our own rendering of Symphosius 61 (Riese 1894). People invented.

An old skipper of the bank is buried in a coffin made of his own boat's planks: coffins of reused ship planking are known from the Dorestad graveyards (Van Es and Verwers; Design/content/ships.md) (?). The dead man, his widow and the prices are invented (rope 10 d, sailcloth 40 d: goods_793.json).

cards.note: Dorestad, the selling on the dams: a feast day at midsummer. The engine's 'feast' in June is Saint John's (24 June, with the fires of the night before) or Saints Peter and Paul (29 June): the game's first feasts, three and eight days after it begins, so the words name midsummer and not the day. In 793 they fall sixteen and twenty-one days after Lindisfarne. Midsummer fires are older than the saint; that Dorestad lit them is a guess (?). No selling before Mass on a feast is the church's rule (capitularies on Sunday and feast markets, e.g. Admonitio generalis 789, c. 81 (?)).

cards.note: Dorestad, the selling on the dams: a salter up from the coast sells grey peat salt by the sack and, with it, a Latin riddle about salt that a monk taught him (riddle_aldhelm_19_salis: thread riddle_road, hook for Dorestad: 'The salt riddle that starts salt_to_pepper may be bought here or at Quentovic'; the story dorestad.first_question beat 4). Aldhelm's riddle 19, 'Sal'; the salter says it in his own words, which are our rendering (Ehwald 1919 for the Latin). Zeeland and Frisian peat salt came up the river to Dorestad (Van Es and Verwers). Salt 3 d the sack, the riddle 12 d (riddles_793.json). The salter is invented; he may be met again at the hearths (harbour.salt_hearths.walichrum).

The three lines are our own plain rendering of Symphosius 4 (Riese 1894); Liudger's books: Altfrid, Vita Liudgeri I.12. The schoolmaster is invented.

cards.note: Traiectum, the prior's store: Hadda (traiectum.cellarer), the 'prior Hadda' of Alcuin's carmen 4, who gives the traveller honey, porridge and butter because 'Frisia pours out neither oil nor wine'. He buys wax at a true weight (flag rf_fair_wax) and knows Hrotberct's short cakes (flag rf_short_wax, from harbour.black_haired_merchant.dorestad). In the famine he has the king's order to feed the starving and no grain (thread hungry_years, hook for Traiectum; sets hy_fed_poor): the order to bishops, abbots and counts is the capitulary of 792-793 (MGH Capit. I no. 21 (?)). Rye at 3 d: the price of Frankfurt 794.

cards.note: Traiectum, the bishop's hall: Hamacar (traiectum.hamacar, cast.hamacar; bishop about 790-806). He will stand surety for a house that has carried for the church or sold to it fairly (sets db_surety: thread counts_day, hook for Traiectum), gives an order for wax, and answers the letter from Daventre about the bell (flags rf_bell_letter, rf_bell_answer; story daventre.one_mass beat 3). Wax for the lights was every church's standing want. Only his name and years are in the sources: the man is invented.

cards.note: Traiectum, the strand: a passenger. Landed by harbour.priest_landed.emuthon. Liudger's return after the rising: Altfrid, Vita Liudgeri I.22 (?). The young priest and the ferryman (traiectum.aldlef) are invented.

cards.note: Traiectum, the guest house: a fast day. In Lent the house eats no meat (the Lenten fast was law for all the baptised: e.g. Capitulatio de partibus Saxoniae c. 4 makes eating meat in Lent a capital matter for Saxons); fish is allowed, and the Vecht gives eels. The guest-master and what he says are invented. The condition is the engine's 'fast', or March.

cards.note: Traiectum, Saint Martin's: the keeper shows the church's plate to those who give alms; among it a cup of old northern work, which the herdsman at Winaldum asks after (harbour.bare_mound.wijnaldum; flags rf_aldward_asked, rf_saw_cup; thread cross_and_grove, hook for Wijnaldum; story wijnaldum.bare_mound beat 2). Liudger breaking shrines in Frisia and sending their treasure, two parts to the king and one to himself by the king's gift: Altfrid, Vita Liudgeri I.16 (?). On Martinmas (11 November) the toll man of Medemelacha brings the bishop's tenth (the Utrecht goods register (?)). The cup is invented.

cards.note: Traiectum, Saint Salvator's: an oath. From 834 the fleets pass under the wall for Dorestad (Annales Bertiniani 834-837); in 857 Northmen waste Utrecht while Rorik is away in Denmark and Bishop Hunger flees (Annales Bertiniani 857; nl.wikipedia 'Hunger (bisschop)'). The canon Odulf (traiectum.odulf, d. about 855) asks skippers for a promise; after him another canon holds them to it. The thread dorestad_falls, hook for Traiectum; the story traiectum.the_chest_goes_inland beats 1 and 3. The chest goes to Daventre (harbour.chest_received.daventre). The promise and the chest are invented.

The thread price_of_england, hook for Traiectum; the story traiectum.our_own_fire beat 3. The merchant (traiectum.bernbod) is invented.

cards.note: Noviomagus, the clerks' bench: the palace clerk (noviomagus.engilbald), a pupil of Alcuin, gives the riddle of the river and the fish (riddle_symphosius_12_flumen: thread riddle_road, hook for Traiectum 'At Noviomagus a clerk of the palace has the river and the fish'; story noviomagus.river_and_fish beats 2 and 4) and WANTS a text: the English riddle on the same matter (exeter_85_fish_river). Alcuin's Disputatio Pippini has this riddle; the three lines are our own rendering of Symphosius 12 (Riese 1894). Alcuin was abbot of Tours from 796 to his death in 804. The clerk is invented.
cards.when: moored and port.id = noviomagus and year < 831

cards.note: Noviomagus, the king's cellar: the keeper of the larder (noviomagus.ratbert) orders wine against the court's coming (a commission), says what the count likes at table (story noviomagus.counts_feast beat 2), and takes the Daventre smith's ironwork (harbour.heath_iron.daventre; flags rf_einbert_load, rf_einbert_silver). A royal estate's stores and what they must hold: Capitulare de villis (c. 800), cc. 42, 62. The people are invented.

Let him lift a sack, and say nothing

cards.note: Noviomagus, the king's house on a feast day: the count (dorestad.folcbert, cast.folcbert) is among his equals, and can be asked to his face for a delay (sets db_extension) or an errand (sets db_service). The thread counts_day, hook for Noviomagus; the story noviomagus.counts_feast beat 4. Charles kept Easter at Nijmegen in 777, 804, 806 and 808 (Annales regni Francorum); that the count of the Dorestad district came is a guess (?). Hounds 36 d, wine 60 d (goods_793.json).

Bow, and say nothing of the debt

memory.wine.failure: gave wine at the king's table

cards.note: Noviomagus, the fort gate: a favour. The king's huntsman (noviomagus.haribrand), a Saxon carried west, asks for word to be taken to the Saxon ale-wife at Daventre (flag rf_haribrand_word, read by harbour.hathugards_question.daventre; thread saxon_end; story daventre.the_counted_son). Saxons were moved west and settled in Francia in 795, 797, 798, 799 and 804 (Annales regni Francorum; Einhard, Vita Karoli 7). He also says when the count's hunt went well (flag rf_hunt_morning; story noviomagus.counts_feast beat 3). Invented people.
cards.when: moored and port.id = noviomagus and year >= 797 and year < 836
cards.title: The huntsman at the gate
cards.intention: A silent man in green and brown stands at the fort gate with two hounds on one leash. He lets three masons pass, and stops you.

options.label: Carry his word to Daventre
Ask him to send word when the hunt has gone well
Buy a haunch for the crew, and ask no questions (5 d)
Nod and go in

cards.note: Noviomagus, the church by the palace: the priest (noviomagus.liudrad) and the hungry on the road (thread hungry_years; story noviomagus.law_in_lent beat 3; sets hy_fed_poor). The law written here in March 806 fixed the prices of grain and named buying cheap at harvest to sell dear 'shameful gain' (Capitulare missorum Niumagae datum, 806, cc. 17-18: oats 2 d, barley 3, spelt 3, rye 4, cleaned wheat 6 the modius). Two sacks at 8 d is that price. The priest and the forty are invented.
cards.when: moored and port.id = noviomagus and (year < 795 or (year >= 805 and year < 808))

priest.note: noviomagus.liudrad

cards.title: Forty on the road
cards.intention: By the old graves below the church people are sitting who belong to no lord: thin, quiet, with their bundles beside them. The priest is among them with an empty basket.

options.label: Give two sacks of rye at the church door
Sell him two sacks at the lawful price (8 d)
Say your hold is the count's before it is yours

memory.sell: sold rye at the lawful price

cards.note: Noviomagus, the landing: what the palace hears. In 836-837 the count of Walcheren's word is brought up the river (from harbour.counts_word.walichrum, flag rf_eggihard_word; story walichrum.the_island_falls beat 2): Walcheren fell on 17 June 837 and the emperor, who had meant to go to Rome, came to Nijmegen and held an inquiry (Annales Bertiniani 837). In 846 the emperor Lothar was at Nijmegen and could not stop the burning of Dorestad (Annales Fuldenses, Xantenses 846): thread dorestad_falls, hook for Noviomagus; story noviomagus.smoke_downriver beat 2. The clerk is invented.
cards.when: moored and port.id = noviomagus and ((flag.rf_eggihard_word and year < 838) or year = 846)

Say nothing and look at the river

cards.note: Daventre, Hathugard's ale-house (daventre.hathugard): a Saxon woman asks every boat about a son given as a hostage in 785 (sets sx_brother_trail: thread saxon_end, hook for Daventre; story daventre.the_counted_son beat 1). He is the brother of the mate Brunger (cast.crew.brunger); the spine finds him at Mogontia about 805 (mogontia.brunric). Hostages by the hundred given to bishops and counts: Annales regni Francorum 794-798; the 'Indiculus obsidum Saxonum' (c. 805) lists Saxon hostages and their keepers. Also takes the huntsman's word from Noviomagus (flag rf_haribrand_word). Invented people.
cards.when: moored and port.id = daventre and year < 807

Say you have seen no such man, and drink

memory.word: brought word from the king's wood

cards.note: Daventre, the host's ground: each spring the king's host crosses the IJssel here for Saxony and its buyers take grain, salt meat and horses (thread saxon_end, hook for Daventre: 'Grain, horses and salt meat are bought up each May for the army'). In 797 ships were hauled by river and overland into Saxony (Annales regni Francorum 797: the king came to Hadeln). A commission for oats. The mate is Brunger (cast.crew.brunger), whose village such a levy burned. The buyer is invented; salt pork 14 d, the count pays 18.
cards.when: moored and port.id = daventre and year < 805 and month >= 4 and month <= 6

Say the boat is bespoke

memory.no: would not sell to the host

cards.note: Daventre, Lebuin's church: the priest (daventre.liudbod) says one Mass for Saxon converts and Frankish soldiers (thread cross_and_grove, hook for Daventre; story daventre.one_mass beat 1) and wants a bell: a letter for the bishop (flag rf_bell_letter, answered by harbour.bishops_hall.traiectum), and the founding paid for (flag unlock_work_daventre_bell; the work daventre.work.bell). Lebuin's church burned by Saxons and rebuilt by Liudger about 776: Altfrid, Vita Liudgeri I.13-15. Bells cast for churches: Walafrid Strabo, De exordiis c. 5 (?). The priest is invented.

cards.note: Daventre, the Heest: the old gods at the edge of a new church (thread cross_and_grove, hook for Daventre; story daventre.one_mass beat 2). Offerings at trees, springs and stones were forbidden to the baptised Saxons (Capitulatio de partibus Saxoniae c. 21: 'ad fontes aut arbores vel lucos votum fecerit'; Indiculus superstitionum cc. 6-11) and went on. The woman and the hollow are invented.
cards.when: moored and port.id = daventre and year < 810 and not flag.rf_heest_seen and not flag.rf_heest_told and not flag.rf_heest_offered

options.label: Leave a penny in the crock
Say nothing, and go down
Sign yourself, and tell her the priest should hear of it

cards.note: Daventre, the forge on the bank: a favour, and a matter of trust. The smith (daventre.einbert) sends three crates of hooks, knives and nails to the keeper of the king's larder at Noviomagus (harbour.kings_cellar.noviomagus), who pays late; the merchant brings back the silver, less a fifth, or does not (deeds kept_commission / broke_commission). Iron smelted from bog and heath ore on the Veluwe was the district's trade (Heidinga, Medieval Settlement and Economy North of the Lower Rhine, 1987). Iron tools 30 d the crate, rivets 16 d the keg (goods_793.json). Invented people.
cards.when: moored and port.id = daventre and year < 813

cards.intention: The forge stands open to the bank so that the smith can see who lands. He looks at your hands before your face.

cards.note: Daventre, Lebuin's church, 857 and after: the chest of Saint Martin's is received (from harbour.odulfs_promise.traiectum; story traiectum.the_chest_goes_inland beat 4; sets traiectum_chest_saved and bk_carried). Bishop Hunger fled Utrecht in 857; Lothar II gave him the monastery of Berg (Sint Odiliënberg) on the Roer in 858, and the bishops later sat at Deventer until about 920 (nl.wikipedia 'Hunger (bisschop)', 'Radboud van Utrecht'). The chest and the lid are invented. Grand reward on the honest road: flag unlock_title_saint_martins_carrier (the church's own carrier).

Keep back one book against the freight

cards.note: Walichrum, Wiltrud's house (walichrum.wiltrud): a rumour that is FALSE. A skipper swears that King Offa is dead and the English ports will open. Offa died on 29 July 796 (Anglo-Saxon Chronicle 796), and the card comes only before that year. Aldswith at Dorestad puts it right (harbour.aldswiths_bench.dorestad reads flag rf_heard_offa_dead). The quarrel of the kings and the shut ports: Gesta abbatum Fontanellensium c. 12; Alcuin to Colcu, 790 (the spine's thread black_stones). Quernstones 12 d the pair in a good year (goods_793.json); ten is a dear price while they lie unsold. Invented people.
cards.when: moored and port.id = walichrum and year < 796
cards.title: News at Wiltrud's house
cards.intention: At Wiltrud's fire a skipper nobody knows is telling the bench something for the third time, louder each time. He sees a new face and begins again.

options.label: Pay his score and thank him (3 d)
Buy two pair of quernstones on the strength of it (20 d)
Ask Wiltrud what she thinks of it

memory.pay: paid for the news that Offa was dead

cards.note: Walichrum, the brooch-maker's hearth (walichrum.wilbraht): the islanders' old small pennies are dead coin after the king's reform (Frankfurt, June 794, c. 5). They can be bought by weight and carried to the mint (harbour.kings_mint.dorestad reads flag rf_old_coin_pot) or to a Dane's scale. The thread silver_road; the story walichrum.old_pennies beats 1 and 2. Domburg's beach has given over a thousand sceattas of the 8th century (Op den Velde and Klaassen, Sceattas and Merovingian Deniers from Domburg and Westenschouwen, 2004). Invented people.
cards.when: moored and port.id = walichrum and year >= 794 and year < 811

options.label: Buy the pot by weight, fairly (30 d)
Tell her they are dead coin, and offer fifteen
Sit with him an afternoon and learn the ring of good silver

cards.note: Walichrum, the king's house, 836 and spring 837: a favour for the count. Witla and Antwerp were burned in 836 (Annales Bertiniani 836); on 17 June 837 the Northmen fell on Walcheren, killed Count Eggihard and Hemming son of Halfdan, and took tribute (Annales Fuldenses 837; Thegan's continuator). The count (walichrum.eggihard) asks for his word to be carried to the palace (flag rf_eggihard_word, delivered by harbour.palace_hears.noviomagus). The thread dorestad_falls, hook for Walichrum; the story walichrum.the_island_falls beat 1. What they say is invented.
cards.when: moored and port.id = walichrum and (year = 836 or (year = 837 and month < 6)) and not flag.rf_eggihard_word and not flag.rf_palace_heard

options.label: Carry his word to Noviomagus
Sell the watch a coil of rope, and wish him luck
Tell him what you saw, and sail on the ebb

memory.leave: told what he saw and sailed

cards.note: Walichrum, the sheep marsh: a favour across the coast. Bernhild (walichrum.bernhild) nurses a sister whose face a sickness has eaten; the wise woman of the Ems (emuthon.notburg) makes a salve that eases and does not mend (harbour.rain_pond.emuthon sets flag rf_salve). The story walichrum.the_side_room, all its beats. The sickness is not named in the period's words: lupus and leprosy were both 'lepra' (?). Cheese 4 d the wheel, honey 24 d the crock (goods_793.json). Invented people.
cards.when: moored and port.id = walichrum and year < 806 and port.visits >= 1
cards.title: The side room
cards.intention: Bernhild sells cheese at the marsh edge with sixty ewes behind her. She buys honey and linen with the silver, and does not eat the one or wear the other.

options.label: Give her the salve from the Ems, and say it will not mend
Give her a crock of honey and take no silver
Buy two wheels of cheese (8 d)
Ask who the linen is for

memory.salve: brought the salve from the Ems
memory.honey: gave honey and took no silver
memory.ask: asked who the linen was for

cards.note: Walichrum, the salt hearths: a deal at the source. Zeeland's salt was made by burning salt-soaked peat and boiling the washed ash ('zelle', 'darink delven'), from the Carolingian period on (Besteman, 'Carolingian Medemblik'; the abbeys' salt rights on the Zeeland islands, e.g. Lorsch 776 (?)). Sea salt 3 d the sack (goods_793.json); two at the hearth. From 841 the island is held by the Dane Harald (Annales Bertiniani 841). The salter is invented.
cards.when: moored and port.id = walichrum and month >= 8 and month <= 11

salter.note: a salter of the marsh; walichrum.unno from 825

options.label: Buy six sacks at the hearth (12 d)
Lend your crew to carry peat for a day, and take salt for it
Taste it, nod, and walk on

cards.note: Witla, the pilot's net shed: Gerlef (witla.gerlef, cast.gerlef), pilot of the Maas mouth, is kept by Thiadbod by the year while the ports are shut, so others wait (thread black_stones; story witla.paid_by_the_year beat 1). A merchant who asks about the water and not the price is in the end taught the marks (flag unlock_pilot_maas; the unlock witla.the_marks). Witla at the Maas mouth: Annales Bertiniani 836; pilots are not recorded there. Invented.
cards.when: moored and port.id = witla and year < 813
cards.title: The pilot's shed
cards.intention: The old pilot sits on a pile of nets in his shed door, looking at the bar. He knows who you are by your boat before he has looked at you.

options.label: Sit on the net pile and ask him about the water
Go out with him at the spring ebb

Wait a tide

memory.double: paid double to be taken over

cards.note: Witla, Saint Peter's farm: the hungry years on an abbey's holding (thread hungry_years; the story witla.five_cows beats 1 and 5; sets hy_fed_poor or hy_sold_dear). A farm 'in Witla' with serfs and cows belonged to Saint Peter's at Ghent (the Liber traditionum of Saint Peter's: the gift of Rathadus (?)); the weaver (witla.thiadlint), her daughter and the eleven pennies are invented. The king's price for rye, three pennies the modius, is Frankfurt 794; a serf's freedom bought with silver is ordinary manumission by the penny (?).
cards.when: moored and port.id = witla and (year < 795 or (year >= 805 and year < 807))

Give her the eleven pennies

cards.note: Witla, Wilsuit's ale-house: skippers waiting on a wind, and dice. Radward (witla.radward) dices for anything and means to be first over the water after any bad news. Bone dice are common finds at Dorestad and on the terps (Roes, Bone and Antler Objects from the Frisian Terp-Mounds, 1963). He tells a true thing: what a cask of Rhine wine fetches at Lundenwic (Design/content/CHAINS.md: about 50 d at Dorestad, 80 d at Lundenwic). Invented people.

Watch the bones and keep your purse shut

cards.note: Medemelacha, the eel stakes: the second of three cards (after harbour.thiadbods_dam.dorestad, before harbour.night_hull.emuthon). Eilbern (medemelacha.eilbern) hands over twelve bundles in the dark; the toll man (medemelacha.radward) counts hulls at first light. The thread swords_north, hook for Medemelacha ('where a cargo changes boats at night'); the story medemelacha.night_boats beats 2 and 3. The cargo is carried as a flag (rf_bundles), not as goods, so that it is never in the market. The king's toll at Medemblik and Saint Martin's tenth of it: the Utrecht goods register (before 866 (?)). Invented people.

Push off and leave him his bundles

memory.take.failure: took the bundles and was seen riding deep

cards.note: Medemelacha, Meinburg's house (medemelacha.meinburg and her daughters after her): the people of a place as a card with memory. She cuts each skipper's mark in her door post and a notch for each return; the lines turn on port.visits and on the generation of the house. The story medemelacha.door_post, beats 1 to 4. Owners' marks cut on wood are common finds in the terps and at Dorestad (Roes 1963) (?); the post is invented. She also tells a true thing about the Almere by night.
cards.when: moored and port.id = medemelacha

Ask what she would not tell a new boat
Sleep aboard

cards.note: Medemelacha, the stone ground: a commission. Tado (medemelacha.tado) dresses rough Mayen lava querns into finished stones; roughouts and waste of Mayen basalt are among the finds of Carolingian Medemblik (Besteman, 'Carolingian Medemblik', BROB 24, 1974). While the kings quarrel the English shore is shut to him (thread black_stones). Quernstones 12 d the pair (goods_793.json). The man is invented.
cards.when: moored and port.id = medemelacha and year < 816

options.label: Take his order: four pair of sound roughouts
Buy a dressed pair he has kept back (10 d)
Knock on a stone, listen, and learn what 'tock' sounds like

cards.note: Winaldum, the bare mound: the old lords' terp (thread cross_and_grove, hook for Wijnaldum: 'an old man who was there as a boy tells it without anger or forgiveness'; the story wijnaldum.bare_mound, beats 1, 2 and 5). Aldward (wijnaldum.aldward) saw a shrine broken and its silver carried off, and asks what became of it; the cup is at Saint Martin's (harbour.saint_martins_plate.traiectum; flags rf_aldward_asked, rf_saw_cup). For a true answer he tells the fight at Finn's hall as the Frisians have it: the Finn episode of Beowulf (beowulf_17, texts_793.json). Liudger and the Frisian shrines: Altfrid, Vita Liudgeri I.16 (?); the Frankish burning of Frisian shrines in 734: Fredegar's continuator c. 17. That a shrine stood at Wijnaldum is invented.
cards.when: moored and port.id = wijnaldum and year < 810

cards.intention: On the second mound a square of grass is left ungrazed. A very old man with a herdsman's staff stands at its edge, and moves to keep you off it.

Tell him it was all melted long ago
Listen, and keep off the grass

cards.note: Winaldum, the head house: an oath before a Frisian court. A man broke into a weaving hut by night and crushed a weaver's hand. The law is real: the hand of a woman who weaves the fine cloth (fresum) is paid for a quarter higher than another's (Lex Frisionum, Iudicia Wlemari 10: 'feminae fresum facienti similiter', beside the harper and the goldsmith); breaking into a 'screona', a weaving hut, by night is a capital matter in the neighbouring law (Lex Saxonum 33). The story wijnaldum.the_weavers_hand beat 3. The head of the house (wijnaldum.folcward), the weaver (wijnaldum.liafburg) and the case are invented.

cards.note: Doccinga, the church of Saint Paul and Saint Boniface: a feast day. Boniface and his companions were killed here on 5 June 754 (Willibald, Vita Bonifatii c. 8); the church on the mound was built soon after, and Liudger served it for seven years from about 777 (Altfrid, Vita Liudgeri I.17-19). The thread cross_and_grove, hook for Doccinga ('his day is kept on the fifth of June. Liudger passes in spring and autumn'); the story doccinga.fifth_of_june beat 2. The engine's feast table does not hold the day, so the card comes in June; in 793 the game begins after it. The priest (doccinga.meinward) is invented. Wine 60 d the cask; the church pays 56.

cards.note: Doccinga, the weaving house at Aalsum: a deal with a memory. Meinhild (doccinga.meinhild) wants not a buyer but the same buyer every year at shearing (flag rf_aalsum_promise, kept or let lapse; deed kept_commission). Frisian cloth ('pallia Fresonica') was the coast's great export (Notker, Gesta Karoli I.34, II.9; Ermoldus Nigellus); sunken weaving huts are known from the terps. Cloth 48 d the bolt (goods_793.json): she asks 44, and 40 of a buyer who comes back. Invented people.

cards.note: Emuthon, the sheep-house on the marsh, 793-794: a passenger. A priest in hiding (emuthon.liafbraht) wants passage west to Traiectum (sets ms_carried_priest). The threads saxon_end and cross_and_grove, hooks for Emuthon; the story emuthon.priest_in_the_sheep_house beats 1 and 2. The host is Tetta (emuthon.tetta). The search at the river mouth is warned of first. Invented people.

Herb-women and their 'ligaturae' are what the church's lists forbid (Indiculus superstitionum c. 10; Admonitio generalis 789 c. 65). Fleeces 8 d the bundle, cheese 4 d (goods_793.json). Invented.

cards.note: The terp country in a hungry year, at Medemelacha, Winaldum, Doccinga or Emuthon: it grows cattle, not corn, buys its bread every year, and in a famine pays in cloth, cheese, hides or a daughter's dowry silver (thread hungry_years, hook for Wijnaldum 'Also at Doccinga, Emuthon and Medemelacha'; the stories medemelacha.bread_for_cloaks, wijnaldum.bread_for_cloth, doccinga.dowry_for_bread and emuthon.bread_for_cloth). Sets hy_fed_poor or hy_sold_dear. The famine of 792-793 and of 805-806: Annales Mosellani 792-793; Capitulare missorum of Thionville 805 c. 4. The king's price, rye three pennies the modius: Frankfurt 794 c. 4. Cheese 4 d, hides 15 d the bundle (goods_793.json). Invented people.

cards.note: Walichrum, the creek strand: a passenger. An English pilgrim bound for Rome has been set ashore by a ship that sells on the mud and will not go up to the toll at Dorestad; he wants passage up the river, where the Rhine road begins. English pilgrims to Rome by the Frankish ports: Boniface landed at Dorestad in 716 (Willibald, Vita Bonifatii c. 4) and crossed by Quentovic in 718; that pilgrims still used the Rhine mouth in the 790s is likely, not recorded (?). The tall-stemmed English ship is the places file's (walichrum.strand). Invented people.

cards.note: Walichrum, where the idol stood: the story walichrum.the_idol, beat 1, and its three endings (flags rf_idol_done, rf_idol_both, rf_idol_named, rf_idol_silent). About 796 Alcuin wrote the Life of Willibrord for Beornrad, abbot of Echternach and archbishop of Sens (d. 797); chapter 14 tells how Willibrord broke an idol on Walcheren and its keeper struck him on the head with a sword and did not hurt him, and died on the third day (Vita Willibrordi, MGH SS rer. Merov. VII). That a monk came asking on the island is invented. The two families' tellings are the places file's (Bernhild is the actor farm_wife, Wilbraht the actor craftsman, as in the island's other cards).

cards.note: Walichrum, the fenced graves: a burying. Bernhild's sister Thiadwih (the story walichrum.the_side_room, beat 4 and the ending 'planks') is laid in a coffin of old boat planks with a penny on her right shoulder, and Bernhild asks whether the planks may come from the merchant's boat. It comes only to a house she counts a friend (rf_bernhild_friend, set by harbour.side_room.walichrum). The Domburg graves: hollowed-trunk and plank coffins, heads to the west, coins on the right shoulder (de Man 1899, as in the places file). Sets rf_thiadwih_buried and, for the planks, rf_island_kin. Invented people.

cards.note: Walichrum, the high dune: weather by the sheep. The boy who watches for sails says Bernhild's ewes lay facing the land this morning, and that nobody on the island sails the day after (walichrum.bernhild's own rumour line). A true omen at doubtful odds, and a true word on the salt season (harbour.salt_hearths.walichrum is open from August to November). Animal weather signs are as old as Aratus and Virgil (Georgics I); this one is invented in that manner. Invented people.

cards.note: Noviomagus, the bank below the wall, in the hungry spring of 806: the story noviomagus.law_in_lent, beats 1 and 2 and its endings (the thread hungry_years). The capitulary given at Nijmegen in March 806 (MGH Capit. I no. 46, c. 17-18) sets the price of the modius at 2 d for oats, 3 for barley, 3 for spelt, 4 for rye and 6 for cleaned wheat, and names as shameful gain the buying of grain at harvest to sell it dear. Ratbert (noviomagus.ratbert, the actor cellarer) buys for the king's table and the king's poor; Engilbald (noviomagus.engilbald, the actor clerk) reads it out. 'Keep the hold shut' sets the story's own flag hy_sold_dear.

cards.note: Noviomagus, Easter 1018: a plaint before the emperor (the story noviomagus.tiel_complaint, beat 2, and its endings). The emperor Henry II kept Easter 1018 at Nijmegen (6 April); the merchants of Tiel complained there that Count Dirk III had built a fort at Vlaardingen and took toll of ships bound for England, and Bishop Adalbold of Utrecht complained with them; an army was sent and was beaten in the ditches at Vlaardingen on 29 July (Thietmar of Merseburg VIII.27-30 (?); Alpertus of Metz, De diversitate temporum II.20-21). Sibrand (noviomagus.tiel_merchant) is invented. Flags rf_tiel_spoke, rf_tiel_stood, rf_dirk_word.

cards.note: Noviomagus, the winter of 880-881: the Northmen hold the king's house behind a rampart and King Louis the Younger's army lies outside in the frost (Annales Fuldenses 880; Regino of Prum 881). Inside is Eberhard the Saxon, son of Count Meginhard, whom his mother Evesa ransomed 'at a great price' (Regino 881; noviomagus.eberhard). The first of three steps: his word goes to harbour.evesas_man.daventre (rf_eberhard_word), the answer comes back here (rf_eberhard_answer), and the house of Meginhard remembers (rf_meginhard_friend). Levison p. 73, as in the places file). The spring of sweet water found when the mound was raised for his church: Willibald, Vita Bonifatii c. 9. The island priest's word about water drawn in silence is Alcuin's account of Fositesland (Vita Willibrordi c. 10), carried here by Landric (emuthon.landric), the chief's son of that island: the story doccinga.fifth_of_june, beat 4. She is real and nameless in the source; her age that morning is invented.

cards.note: Doccinga, June 873: the story doccinga.oostergos_answer, beat 3, and its endings. Rodulf, a Dane of the royal kin who had taken tribute on many coasts, sent to Oostergo for his; the Frisians answered that they owed tribute to none but King Louis and his sons, fought, and killed him and many of his men (Annales Fuldenses 873 says eight hundred (?); Annales Bertiniani 873 five hundred and more). The rest were shut in a building; a Northman long a Christian and settled among the Frisians advised taking their treasure, hostages and their oath never to come back into King Louis's kingdom (Annales Fuldenses 873; doccinga.northman). An oath, and a commission of a kind: carry the word south (rf_rodulf_news, to harbour.rodulf_is_dead.daventre) or weigh the treasure for a tenth (the ending 'silver': about 250 d; rf_rodulf_weighed). Count Albdag led the Frisians (Annales Fuldenses); Aldbern (doccinga.lords_man) is invented.

cards.note: Emuthon, the sand the tide covers, in the year of the rising: the thread saxon_end, hook for Emuthon; the story emuthon.the_rising, beat 1. The free men meet in a ring on ground that is nobody's; a boat from a Frankish port is asked whose man her master is. An oath card: what is said in the ring is remembered on the mound for a generation (the memory of the actor lawman). That the assembly met on the tidal sand is the places file's and invented; assemblies at the shore are attested for later Frisia only (?). Invented people.

Her words here are ours, after Rimbert. Catla is the spine's cast.catla (birka.catla); the year is not known (about 852 (?)). The woman of the bank is Aldswith's granddaughter Aldgard (dorestad.aldgard; the easter egg at dorestad.lodging); that a shipman walked beside the bag is invented.

cards.note: Walichrum, the ring wall, after the raid: 838 to 850. On 17 June 837 the Northmen fell on the island, killed Count Eggihard and Hemming and led many women away captive (Annales Bertiniani, Fuldenses and Xantenses 837); on Saint Stephen's day 838 the sea covered nearly all Frisia (Annales Bertiniani 839). The ring forts of sods on the Zeeland islands are of the 9th century; whether Domburg's was begun as early as 838 is disputed (the places file; some date it after 851 or about 890) (?). Unno (walichrum.unno) and his sister Berntrud are the places file's; the promise to ask after her (flag rf_berntrud_asked) is left for the Danish markets (the story walichrum.the_island_falls, beat 5, at Sliesthorp). The work walichrum.work.wall_share (flag unlock_work_walichrum_wall_share).

Swearing to Rorik's peace sets the thread's flag df_rorik_man. Rorik is dorestad.rorik (cast.rorik); Dorestad itself has been dead since 863, and he holds the counties round it. The palace begun by King Charles at Nijmegen: Einhard, Vita Karoli 17. Tar for the seams came from the pine country far up the Rhine and was always short (our guess (?)); tar 20 d the barrel in goods_793.json, 24 here. Invented people.

cards.note: Noviomagus, Pentecost 1036: a feast day. Henry, son of the emperor Conrad, wedded Gunhild, daughter of King Cnut, at Nijmegen at Pentecost (6 June 1036); she took the name Kunigunde and was crowned on the feast of the Apostles, 29 June (Wipo, Gesta Chuonradi c. 35; the dossier). Cnut had died at Shaftesbury on 12 November 1035 and lay at Winchester (Anglo-Saxon Chronicle 1035); his sons shared and disputed his kingdoms. Under him the tolls on the road to Rome had been eased for English and Danish merchants (his letter of 1027). The buyers, the crews and the prices are invented (wine 60 d in goods_793.json; 85 at a king's wedding).

Red dots round the great letters are a mark of the Insular hands, as in the Lindisfarne Gospels (about 700). cards.note: Traiectum after the return of the see, 920 to 975: Bishop Balderik (traiectum.balderik), who brought the bishops home from Daventre about 920 and rebuilt the churches, the school and the walls (the dossier traiectum; nl.wikipedia 'Balderik van Utrecht'). The thread dorestad_falls; the story traiectum.the_chest_goes_inland, beat 4 and the ending carried_it: a house whose forefather carried the church's chest inland in 857 (flag traiectum_chest_saved, from harbour.chest_received.daventre) is given ground on the Stathe without rent (flag unlock_plot_traiectum; the unlock traiectum.stathe_ground). King Henry's youngest son Bruno, born 925, was sent to Balderik's school at the age of four (Ruotger, Vita Brunonis c. 4). Lead 15 d the pig, oak 30 d the load in goods_793.json; the orders and prices are invented.

cards.note: Traiectum, Adelbold's cathedral, from 1023: a feast-day card for the later town, and a king's burial. The cathedral and the bishop's house burned in 1017; the new church was hallowed on 26 June 1023 before the emperor Henry II and twelve bishops (the dossier traiectum). Bishop Adelbold wrote to Pope Sylvester on the volume of a sphere (the easter egg at traiectum.school). The emperor Conrad II died at Utrecht on 4 June 1039, the Monday of Pentecost; his body went up the Rhine to Speyer and his entrails stayed in the cathedral (Wipo, Gesta Chuonradi c. 39; the easter egg at traiectum.dom, the stone cut with 'exta'). The condition is the engine's 'feast', or June of 1023 or 1039. The canon is invented; wine 60 d the cask (goods_793.json), 58 here.

The thread counts_day, the spine's hook for Traiectum ('After Dorestad is gone the house's reckoning day is here or at Daventre') and the story traiectum.the_bishops_word, beat 5: a delay asked of him sets db_extension, 'one time only for each creditor'. King Zwentibold's ruling of 896 on the freedom 'they had at Dorestad': Oorkondenboek Sticht Utrecht I no. 88. Parchment 60 d the bundle (goods_793.json). His words are invented, after his own verses.

cards.note: Daventre, the mint, 990 to 1024: the thread silver_road in its last age; the story daventre.the_hand_penny, beats 0, 2 and 4, and its endings 'followed' and 'informer'. About 990 the first pennies were struck here, reading ODDO REX and DAVNERA; Countess Adela of Hamaland struck a penny with the English king's Hand on one side and Deventer's cross on the other, and after 1014 the king's mint struck the Hand type itself (the dossier daventre: Canon van Deventer; 'Munten van gravin Adela', Jaarboek voor Munt- en Penningkunde 67, 1980); the Hand is King Aethelred's type of the 980s. Deventer pennies went north and east and are found pecked and cut in the hoards there. A man who knows the northern reckoning (the thread's flag sv_scale, or rf_two_weights) can tell the moneyer where his coins go. Hrotmar is daventre.hrotmar; the years of the countess's penny are approximate (?).

cards.note: Daventre, Lebuin's feast, the morrow of Martinmas (12 November): a feast-day card for every age of the town. Lebuin (Liafwin), an English priest, went among the Saxons and spoke before their assembly at Marklo; he died here about 773 (Vita Lebuini antiqua, 9th or 10th century, LATER; Altfrid, Vita Liudgeri I.13-15). His church was burned twice by Saxons and a third time by the Northmen in 882; Bishop Bernold built the stone basilica about 1040 (the dossier daventre). The engine's feast table does not hold the day, so the card comes in November. 'Three times built, twice burned' is the places file's saying. The priest is daventre.liudbod to 818 and his successors after.

cards.note: Medemelacha, the king's ground, at Martinmas: a commission of trust, in three steps (here; harbour.tenth_counted.traiectum; here again). The toll man Radward (medemelacha.radward) carries Saint Martin's tenth of the king's tenth to Traiectum himself each Martinmas, and his boat leaks (his own line 'trust'). 'In Medemolaca regalis decima': the goods register of Saint Martin's, about 918 (the dossier medemelacha, WAR 61 2.2.2.1). Carried whole, it earns his cut stick: the house passes this ground untolled (flag unlock_charter_medemelacha; the unlock medemelacha.charter_toll). The tenth is carried as the flag rf_saints_tenth, not as goods. What it holds is invented. The first step comes only in October and November; the return in any month.

cards.note: Medemelacha, the king's ground in the Danes' years, 850 to 873: the people of a place as a card with memory. From 841 to 885 Danish lords held western Frisia by the Frankish kings' gift (Annales Bertiniani 841, 850; Annales Fuldenses 850, 882-885); that Rorik held this toll is likely, not stated (the dossier medemelacha, WAR 61 2.3.3). Gunnulf (medemelacha.gunnulf) weighs where the last man counted. In 867 the people the annals call Cokingi drove Rorik out of Frisia (Annales Bertiniani 867). About 850 and again about 880 silver went into the ground at Westerklief on Wieringen (hoards_793.json 'westerklief'): a friend of his is told where to look (flag rf_west_cliff, open_fetch westerklief; the unlock medemelacha.west_cliff). No Dane is recorded as living here; the man is invented.

cards.note: Medemelacha, the king's ground, 985 to 994: Count Ansfried (medemelacha.ansfried), to whom the child king Otto III gave the king's share of toll, mint and rent at 'villa Medemelacha' on 26 June 985 (the dossier medemelacha, WAR 61 2.2.2.2); two months later at Nijmegen Count Dirk II was given his fief between the two streams as his own (noviomagus.dirk). In 995 Ansfried became bishop of Traiectum and took the toll to Saint Martin's with him. No mint ever worked here (the easter egg at medemelacha.toll). His seal on the house's freedom of the toll is the places file's unlock medemelacha.charter_toll (flag unlock_charter_medemelacha). That he came here himself is not recorded (?); his words are invented. Olive oil 40 d the jar, wax 40 d the cake (goods_793.json).

cards.note: Winaldum, the cross on the terp, 800 to 809: Landric (emuthon.landric, cast.landric), son of a chief of Fosite's island, baptised by Liudger, made a priest and 'for many years set over the teaching of the Frisians' (Altfrid, Vita Liudgeri I.22). The thread cross_and_grove; the story wijnaldum.bare_mound, beat 3, and its endings cross_raised and told_true: he wants a cross on the bare mound itself, and the old herdsman Aldward (wijnaldum.aldward) guards the square where the shrine's posts stood. A merchant who told Aldward the truth about the cup (flag rf_aldward_told, from harbour.bare_mound.wijnaldum) is heard by him. On Fosite's island no one touched the god's cattle and water was drawn in silence: Alcuin, Vita Willibrordi c. 10. That a shrine stood at Winaldum is the game's (?). The work wijnaldum.work.mass_house.

cards.note: Winaldum, the head house in the tribute years, 846 to 867: the thread dorestad_falls; the story wijnaldum.silver_in_the_sod, beats 1 and 2, and its endings kept_faith and told; the unlock wijnaldum.keepers_share ('one penny in twelve'). In 846 the Northmen laid waste Ostracia and Westracia and held nearly the whole province (Annales Xantenses 846); in 850 Rorik was given Dorestad and other counties, and in 867 the Cokingi drove him out of Frisia (Annales Bertiniani 850, 867). Pennies copying the emperor Lothar's Dorestad coin were struck on this coast and buried in number at Tzummarum, a short walk along the ridge (Coupland, 'Dorestad in the ninth century: the numismatic evidence', 1988 (?)). Eilrad (wijnaldum.eilrad), the pot and the Dane's counter are invented.

cards.note: Winaldum, the weaving huts: a deal with a memory, and a favour across the coast (with harbour.house_with_the_looms.emuthon). Liafburg (wijnaldum.liafburg) and her cousin Tetta on the Ems (emuthon.tetta) 'send each other dye and gossip by the same boats': madder east (flag rf_liafburgs_madder), woad back west (flag rf_tettas_blue). Sunken weaving huts on the terp: Journal of Archaeology in the Low Countries 2011; 'pallia Fresonica': Notker, Gesta Karoli I.34, II.9. The yellow thread in her selvedge is the story wijnaldum.the_weavers_hand's. Woad and madder as the dyes of the blue and red cloth are our reading (both are in goods_793.json). Cloth 48 d the bolt in goods_793.json: she asks 44, and 40 of a friend. Invented people.

cards.note: Doccinga, the spring on the mound, 820 to 836: an oath, and a passenger. In the first half of the 9th century a cleric of Utrecht asked here about Boniface, and a very old woman swore she had been present and had seen him cover his head with a gospel book when the sword came down (the Utrecht Life, Vita altera Bonifatii, ed. Levison p. 73; the dossier doccinga). The book shown at Fulda with the cuts in it holds tracts and no gospels (the easter egg at doccinga.spring). She is real and nameless in the source: Adelsuit (doccinga.adelsuit) is the places file's name. The unlock doccinga.old_womans_oath. That she asked for a witness from outside, the clerk's passage and the fare are invented.

cards.note: Doccinga, the Northman's farm, 850 to 872: the people of a place as a card with memory. cards.note: Doccinga, Count Bruno's mint, 1038 to 1057: the later town. Under Bruno of Brunswick, count in the Frisian districts from 1038, pennies were struck at Dokkum, Leeuwarden, Bolsward and Stavoren reading DOCC and BRVN with the king's crowned head; they are found as far as the Baltic lands and Russia (the dossier doccinga; en.numista.com/48388). Bruno was killed on 26 June 1057 (nl.wikipedia 'Bruno II van Brunswijk'). The thread silver_road in its last age. Gerbrand (doccinga.gerbrand) is invented; the unlock doccinga.new_pennies (flag rf_gerbrands_count). The count's due of eight pennies in the pound is our figure (?).

cards.note: Emuthon, the creek mouth, in the second hungry time, 805 to 807: the thread hungry_years's flag hy_ran_grain ('he carried grain out of the realm in a famine year against the law of 805'), set here where the realm stops. The capitulary of Thionville, 805, c. 4: in the present famine each is to help his own as he can and not sell his corn too dear, 'and let no food be sold outside our empire' (MGH Capit. I no. 44). The lawful price of rye in 806 is four pennies the measure (Capitulare missorum Niumagae datum, 806, c. 18); nine by weight is the north-bound hull's price and invented. Folcger (emuthon.folcger) and Tetta (emuthon.tetta) are the places file's. Selling on the mound instead sets hy_fed_poor.

cards.note: Emuthon, the count's die, 1020 to 1051: the thread silver_road in its last age; the story emuthon.light_pennies, beat 0, and the unlock emuthon.two_weights (flag rf_two_weights). From about 1020 to about 1051 pennies were struck here with the names HERIMAN and AMVTHON, light, three quarters of a gram (the dossier emuthon: Giesen 2008; Dannenberg 772-773). The story emuthon.bread_for_cloth, beat 3: two hundred years on, the woman of the house with the looms keeps cloth back for the heirs of a house that sold corn fairly in a famine (reads the thread hungry_years's flag hy_fed_poor; flag rf_imma_cloth). An undated fire burned houses on the mound (Grimm 2010). Imma (emuthon.imma) and her husband the moneyer are invented.

cards.note: Emuthon, the count's post, 1047 to 1063: an oath of a kind, in the last age of the game. The counts of Werl, a Westphalian house, held the county of the Ems; Archbishop Adalbert of Hamburg and Bremen was granted mints and markets over the river at Winsum and Garrelsweer (1047-1057) and in 1062 the king ordered the county itself handed to him; Count Bernhard did not give it up, and about 1063 the archbishop's man Gottschalk was killed (the dossier emuthon: Giesen 2008; Adam of Bremen III (?)). The story emuthon.light_pennies, beat 3, and the ending spoke_for_the_count (flag unlock_charter_emuthon (?), the places file's unlock). The count's man and his stick are invented.
